questions.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choices.①: Why Cities Should Ban Empty Lots
choices.②: Community Gardens: More Than Just Fresh Food
choices.③: How to Grow Vegetables Without Water
choices.④: The Hidden Costs of Urban Farming
choices.⑤: Teaching Children to Cook Healthy Meals

groups.passage: In many large cities, empty lots that once collected trash are being turned into community gardens. Neighbors who had never spoken to each other now work side by side, planting vegetables and sharing tools. Studies show that these gardens do more than provide fresh food. People who garden together report lower stress and a stronger sense of belonging to their neighborhood. Children learn where their food comes from, and older residents pass on knowledge that might otherwise be lost. Some gardens even donate part of their harvest to local food banks. City officials have noticed another benefit: areas with active gardens tend to have less crime, probably because more people are out on the streets caring for the space. Of course, gardens need time, water, and volunteers to survive. Still, the results suggest that a small piece of land can help build a stronger community.

questions.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

choices.①: 의지력을 기르는 훈련이 습관 형성의 첫 단계이다.
choices.②: 성공한 사람들은 대체로 실패에서 더 많은 것을 배운다.
choices.③: 스마트폰 사용 시간을 줄이면 학업 성취도가 높아진다.
choices.④: 좋은 습관을 들이려면 의지에 의존하기보다 주변 환경을 바꾸는 것이 효과적이다.
choices.⑤: 건강한 식습관은 규칙적인 운동과 함께할 때 유지된다.

groups.passage: People often blame a lack of willpower when they fail to build good habits. But researchers suggest that the real problem is usually the environment, not the person. If cookies are on the kitchen counter, you will probably eat them, no matter how strongly you decided to eat healthier. If your phone is next to your bed, checking it will feel like the easiest thing to do. Successful people are not always more disciplined; instead, they tend to arrange their surroundings so that the right choice becomes the easy choice. A student who wants to study more can keep only the textbook on the desk and leave the phone in another room. Someone who wants to eat more fruit can put it in a bowl at eye level. Small changes like these reduce the need for self-control, which is a limited resource. So rather than fighting yourself every day, it is wiser to redesign the place where you live and work.

questions.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

choices.①: Boredom: A Hidden Source of Creativity
choices.②: Why Modern Life Makes Us Bored
choices.③: Ways to Fill Your Free Time

groups.passage: Most of us try to escape boredom as quickly as possible by reaching for a phone or turning on the TV. However, psychologists have found that boredom may actually help the mind. When nothing around us demands attention, the brain begins to wander, connecting ideas that seem unrelated. In one experiment, people who had completed a dull task, such as copying phone numbers, came up with more creative uses for ordinary objects than those who had not. Many writers and inventors also say that their best ideas arrived during quiet, empty moments, like a long walk or a boring train ride. Of course, constant boredom is not healthy. But in a world full of notifications, a little empty time may be exactly what a creative mind needs.

groups.passage: When facing a difficult problem, many of us prefer to work alone because we think it is faster. However, research on problem solving shows that groups often reach better solutions than even the smartest individual in them. Each member brings different experiences and ways of thinking, so mistakes that one person misses can be spotted by another. In one study, teams that included people from various backgrounds came up with more creative answers than teams of similar people. Of course, a group works well only when its members listen to one another. But when they do, the results speak for themselves. That is why the old saying, "______________________," continues to be true.

questions.q: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

groups.passage: Many people imagine that memory works like a video camera that records events and plays them back exactly as they happened. In fact, memory works more like a storyteller. Each time we remember an event, we do not simply replay it; instead, we ______________ it from pieces of information stored in different parts of the brain. During this process, missing details are filled in by guesses, and new information can sneak in. This is why two people who experienced the same event often remember it differently, and why we can be completely sure about a memory that is partly wrong.

questions.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

groups.passage:
Many people believe that talent alone decides who becomes a great musician. However, a famous study suggests that the truth is more complicated.

(A) The results were clear. By the age of twenty, the top violinists had practiced about 10,000 hours, far more than the other groups.

(B) This does not mean that talent is meaningless. It does show, however, that without long and focused practice, talent alone is rarely enough.

(C) Psychologist Anders Ericsson and his colleagues compared violin students at a music academy in Berlin. They divided the students into groups according to their level, from the best to the average, and then asked each group how many hours they had practiced.

choices.②: 노인은 지폐 두 장이 붙은 채로 돈을 냈다.
choices.④: 사장은 여분의 돈을 가져도 된다고 말했다.

groups.passage: Last winter, my friend Jiwoo worked part-time at a small bakery. One snowy evening, an elderly man bought a loaf of bread for 4,000 won and handed her what looked like a single 10,000-won bill. Jiwoo gave him 6,000 won in change, and he left. When she tidied the cash drawer, she found that the bill was really two bills stuck together; the man had paid 20,000 won by mistake. Her boss, who was counting the day's sales, said, "Nobody saw it. You can keep the extra 10,000 won." But Jiwoo shook her head, put on her coat, and ran into the snow. She found the man waiting at the bus stop and gave him the money back. He smiled and said, "Thank you. I was too tired to notice." When she returned, her boss said nothing, but he handed her a warm cup of milk.

questions.q:
주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

As a result, many of them end up on roads instead of in the water.

groups.passage: Sea turtles hatch at night on sandy beaches and must reach the ocean on their own. ( ① ) By instinct, they crawl toward the brightest horizon, which, under natural conditions, is the open sea reflecting moonlight and starlight. ( ② ) Today, however, bright lights from hotels, streets, and houses often shine on the beaches. ( ③ ) The hatchlings mistake these lights for the sea and move in the wrong direction. ( ④ ) Many die from exhaustion, from dehydration, or under the wheels of cars. ( ⑤ ) Some coastal towns have therefore asked residents to switch off outdoor lights during the hatching season.

questions.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 <u>않은</u> 것은?

groups.passage: There are many simple ways to reduce the water we use at home. First, turning off the tap while you brush your teeth can <u>ⓐsave</u> dozens of liters every day. Second, repair leaking pipes quickly, because even a small leak can <u>ⓑwaste</u> thousands of liters a year. Taking short showers instead of long baths is also <u>ⓒineffective</u>. Another tip is to run the washing machine only when it is full, which helps <u>ⓓreduce</u> the amount of water used per load. Finally, collecting rainwater for your garden is a smart way to <u>ⓔprotect</u> clean drinking water.

questions.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Praising children for their (A) ______ rather than their (B) ______ helps them take on challenges with confidence.

groups.passage: Parents and teachers often praise children by saying, "You're so smart!" It sounds kind, but research suggests it may backfire. In one well-known experiment, fifth graders solved easy puzzles and were praised either for their intelligence or for their effort. When offered a choice between a harder task and an easier one, most of the children praised for intelligence chose the easier task. They seemed afraid that failure would prove they were not smart after all. In contrast, the majority of the children praised for effort chose the harder task, because they believed that struggling was part of learning. Later, when given difficult problems, the effort group kept trying longer and enjoyed the work more. The results suggest that how we praise children shapes how they face challenges.

questions.q: 다음 글을 읽고, 정보 과잉으로 인한 압박감에 대처하는 방법을 찾아서 우리말로 쓰시오. (선생님이 채점해요)

groups.passage: We live in an age of endless information, and it is easy to feel overwhelmed. A useful way of coping is to decide in advance what you really need to know. For example, if you are preparing a presentation on climate change, you do not have to read every article online. Instead, choose two or three trusted sources and set a time limit for your research. When the time is up, stop searching and start organizing what you have found. This habit protects your attention and keeps you from drifting from link to link. As a result, you save time and make clearer decisions.

questions.q:
다음 글의 요지를 우리말 20자 내외로 쓰시오.
<조건> cost, decision의 우리말 의미가 포함되어야 함 (선생님이 채점해요)

groups.passage: Imagine you buy a movie ticket for 12,000 won, but ten minutes into the film you realize it is terrible. Should you stay? Many people do, saying, "I already paid for it." This is known as the sunk cost effect: we continue an action simply because we have already spent money, time, or effort on it, even when quitting would be wiser. The money is gone either way, so the only sensible question is whether the next two hours will be enjoyable. Companies fall into the same trap when they keep funding a failing project because they have already invested millions. Governments do so as well. Economists advise that decisions should be based on future costs and benefits, not on what has already been spent.
